$comment: P5c‑2 — the bill register's two shared rules, as a table both repos run.
`planBillSettlement` is what the reference grid draws: how much of each
selected bill this voucher closes, and — when it cannot — the sentence the
operator is shown. Every message here is user-facing, so the check compares
the TEXT, not only the verdict: a mirror that agrees about whether to refuse
and disagrees about why leaves one wording on the screen and another in the
`billSettlementSign` is the smaller rule underneath it, and the reason the
grid can offer a bill no document made (D-55's opening balance): it reads the
side the bill was POSTED on, where `settlementRole` can only switch on a
`TrxType`. Its four rows are the whole fact space.
A case's `given` holds arrays; the cross-product is expanded by the checker,
so one hand-written case is a statement about a REGION.

messages.empty: Select at least one document to settle.
messages.mixed: A single voucher cannot mix supplier (payable) and customer (receivable) documents.
messages.closed: One of the selected documents has nothing left to settle.
messages.refund: The selected returns are a refund — record them on a ${opposite} voucher instead.
messages.exceedsReturns: The selected returns exceed the invoices — collect the difference on a ${opposite} voucher.

sign.why: A receipt credits the party, so it settles what debits them — an invoice, or a customer's opening balance.
A credit note credits the customer, the same way the receipt does; it offsets the collection rather than being settled by it.
A payment debits the party, so it settles what credits them — a purchase, or a supplier's opening balance.
A debit note debits the supplier, the same way the payment does.

plan.why: A voucher MAY name no bill (P5c‑1), but that is the caller short-circuiting before it gets here; asked to plan an empty selection, the rule still says so.
Checked before anything about the bills, so the message is about what the caller actually got wrong.
The ordinary case, and 2,759 of the 2,759 approved vouchers on the development books are this shape.
§3.6's 'Agst Ref rows for every open bill oldest-first' — the feed is sorted, and the fill follows the order given rather than re-sorting.
A note is consumed in full and the cash clears the rest — the arithmetic BUG-0070 is about, seen from the settlement side rather than the register's.
A selection of returns alone is a refund; it belongs on the other voucher, and the message names which.
Distinct from `notes-only`: there IS an invoice, it is just smaller than the credit standing against it.
The cap is the NET of the selection, and the message states the number — which is what the entry screen shows beside the amount box.
One voucher cannot settle a customer and a supplier at once. After D3 a party has ONE ledger, so this arises from the DOCUMENTS rather than from the bills' ledger.

A bill with no document has no control side to state. `null` must read as 'not known', never as a second side — otherwise an opening balance beside an invoice would refuse for a reason that is not true.
The feed drops a fully-settled bill, so reaching this means the caller sent one anyway — an edit whose target closed underneath it.
Cash short of the bill leaves the rest open; the remainder of the LINE is what becomes advance/on-account, and that is a different question (`unappliedRemainder`).
